notes: The 10-year US interest rate (5.15%) is 1.03% above the 3-month rate (4.12%), a normal gap that has changed little in 3 months.
Copper has gained 6.2% on gold over 3 months. Copper follows factory and building demand, while gold is bought in worrying times, so this points to stronger growth.
Oil is down 16% in 6 months: lower costs for businesses, but often a sign of weaker demand.
The US stock market (S&P 500) is above its average price over the last 200 trading days (about 10 months): its long-term uptrend is intact.

todaysConditions.note: The US dollar has risen 3.8% against major currencies over 3 months. Gains made abroad shrink when converted back to dollars, and countries that borrowed in dollars find the debt harder to repay.
Chip-maker shares did 14.5% worse than world stocks over 3 months: a drag on tech-heavy markets.
